claims.text: The starting material is HfZrTiTa0.53.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
Powder metallurgy or controlled casting followed by cold work and annealing can incorporate a uniformly dispersed small volume fraction of HfO2 or ZrO2 nanoparticles into the alloy.
The proposed processing will produce uniformly distributed nano-oxide particles in a refined matrix.
The nano-oxide particles will obstruct dislocation motion.
The nano-oxide particles will promote activation of secondary deformation mechanisms.
The nano-oxides will stimulate additional dislocation generation or twinning.
Obstructed glide and additional dislocation generation or twinning will increase dynamic strain hardening.
Increased dynamic strain hardening will retard strain localization.
Retarded localization will make deformation more uniform and delay catastrophic failure under rapid loading.
Oxide dispersion strengthening will increase yield strength by approximately 10–20% relative to the stated baseline.
Oxide dispersion strengthening will increase compressive strength by approximately 10–20% relative to the stated baseline.
The modified alloy will have a dynamic fracture strain greater than the 13.5% quasi-static baseline value.
The modified alloy will have greater resistance to dynamic strain localization and failure than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy will exhibit a more gradual impact-induced energy-release profile than the baseline alloy.
The prediction applies to adiabatic deformation at strain rates of approximately 1000–5000 s^-1 at room temperature.
The magnitude of improvement depends on the uniformity and stability of the nano-oxide dispersion.
Processing-induced changes in phase stability or grain structure may also affect the measured properties.
